editorial.headline: Technical Skills Training, Organised by Companies
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85581 covers company-run technical training across industrial, construction, automotive and building-services disciplines, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85581 is the classification for company-organised technical vocational training: practical instruction intended to deepen skills and expertise rather than merely introduce a subject. Its terrain is broad but coherent—production machinery, industrial welding and fabrication, metal casting and CNC work; light vehicles, motorcycles and heavy equipment; electrical installation, industrial automation, mechatronics and telecommunications; as well as refrigeration, air-conditioning, construction, surveying, furniture and related technical trades. The defining feature is not one particular discipline, but the delivery of work-oriented technical training by a company.

That breadth matters because the activity is rooted in applied capability. The record describes instruction in disciplines that sit close to workshops, sites, equipment and specialised technical practice: piping installation, sheet-metal work, underwater welding, instrumentation and control, audio-video systems, concrete and masonry construction, timber construction, light-steel work, gypsum work and reinforcement, among others. A business registering this activity is therefore framed as an organiser of training designed to add practical competence in those fields.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. It does not list any open business-scale categories, so this classification should not be presented as carrying a stated scale allocation in the source record.

Bali requires a more location-conscious reading, but not because this activity is blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium. The Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and the record identifies it as medium-high or high risk; it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium that applies island-wide to low and medium-low risk activities. The practical instruction is equally clear: verify the position for the specific address. For a foreign-owned company planning technical training in Bali, the national ownership position remains fully open, while the local registration assessment should be checked at the intended premises.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this is a fully foreign-open technical-training activity; in Bali, it is not moratorium-blocked but should be verified for the specific address.
